::: {#rem-congruence-notation}
#### Two meanings of $\equiv$, and the mod operator

The symbol $\equiv$ also means logical equivalence (@def-logical-equivalence).
The "$(\operatorname{mod} n)$" after it says which meaning is in use:
$23 \equiv 8 \pmod{5}$ is a statement about two integers,
and $P \equiv Q$ is a statement about two propositions.

Congruence is related to the mod operator of a programming language,
but it is not the same thing.
In Racket, `(modulo 23 5)` is the number $3$,
while $23 \equiv 8 \pmod{5}$ is a proposition (@def-proposition), which is true or false.

:::
